Container.Name: NextDash
Container.DonateText: Find NextDash useful? Consider supporting the project.
Container.Overview:
NextDash is a lightweight, self-hosted bookmark dashboard that features a minimalist, keyboard-driven interface with extensive customization options, making it the perfect personal dashboard for power users. Based on the excellent ThinkDashboard.
Key features: • Keyboard-driven navigation for fast access to all your bookmarks • Extensive theme and layout customization, with a look studio beside the dashboard and a theme editor • Inbox to collect new links fast: triage them, or keep them under Bookmarks → Unsorted and file whole groups later • Bookmarks view with Health built in: finds broken, stale and duplicate links, with uptime monitoring and downtime alerts • Video bookmarks marked in the list, and played in the hover card without leaving the dashboard • Widgets beside your bookmarks: 36 built-in kinds (uptime, feeds, weather, calendar, disks, containers and more) plus a Custom widget for any JSON API • Your media stack on the dashboard: Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Seerr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd, with the posters from your own library • Finds the web apps in your Docker containers and offers them as bookmarks, with an icon and a status check (needs the Docker socket below) • Your Unraid server on the dashboard: seven widgets for the array, parity, shares, VMs, the UPS and notifications, with alerts • Web search in the search panel through your own SearXNG or the Brave Search API • Six interface languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Chinese • Lightweight and fast, no heavy dependencies • Actively maintained with regular releases
Links: • Website: https://www.nextdash.cc • Source code and releases: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash • Changelog: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/releases • Devlog / release updates: https://www.nextdash.cc/news • Also available on GHCR: ghcr.io/jordibrouwer/nextdash:latest • User manual: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/blob/main/MANUAL.md
The host widgets (Processor, Memory, Disks, Containers) are off until you fill in the optional paths and variables below — they are hidden under Show more settings. Section 15.4 of the manual explains what each one reads.
Support: open an issue on GitHub via the Support link above. Bug reports and feature requests are welcome.
Container.Changes:
### v1.19.9 (2026-10-17) - Containers: nextDash finds the web apps in your Docker containers and offers them as bookmarks; a container that turns up later is asked about first - Containers: the labels nextdash.url, nextdash.name, nextdash.category, nextdash.icon and nextdash.hide steer what is found - First start: a fresh install starts with 98 example links on two pages, or empty if you choose, on the new Slate theme - Import: an import asks whether the bookmarks go onto the dashboard or into the inbox first - Appearance: code, addresses and shortcuts use Source Code Pro - Fixes: clicking the search hint runs that search, and read and unread in the inbox follow the server across devices
### v1.19.8 (2026-10-15) - Widgets: now playing tiles for Jellyfin, Emby and Plex, and Emby and Plex tiles of what was added lately (Plex is read through Tautulli) - Tags: Shift + T opens the tag view of every bookmark, with a Without tags filter - Tag suggestions: Find tags works in the inbox, what you turned down is easy to find again, and self-hosted apps are recognised by name - Tag suggestions: thousands more sites and dozens of new subjects in the catalogue - Dashboard: the page filter stays at the top on a phone - Fixes: Keep settings on this device only keeps them on this device, and media tiles refresh without the Loading line
### v1.19.7 (2026-10-14) - Appearance: nine tabs in three groups (Look, Bookmarks, Header & bars), with link previews on a tab of their own - Appearance: panels fold to one line that says what they are set to, and long tabs list their panels - Appearance: runs of show/hide switches are one row of chips, and rarely used sliders sit under Fine-tune - Action bar: five button sizes, from extra small to extra large; the header destinations grow with them - Tags: subjects in a tree, and new links are looked up on Wikidata quietly, offered as a chip and never written - Fixes: a docked action bar no longer slides into place on a load, and a tab reached through Find settings stays put
### v1.19.6 (2026-10-14) - Tags: a quieter tag cloud with counts and type-to-find; picking a tag opens a table of every bookmark with it, from all pages - Tag suggestions: a catalogue of some 51,000 sites, a Wikidata lookup for unknown ones, and suggestions right in the Bookmarks, tag and Inbox rows - Widgets: a Home Assistant widget for up to 60 entities of your choice - Dashboard: a three-line key legend under the grid (Shift + Z), and Shift + K replays the tour - Tours: shorter tours, at most one tip a day, and settings for animation speed - Fixes: saves from two devices no longer overwrite each other's pages, categories or finders
### v1.19.5 (2026-10-12) - Widgets: Sonarr and Radarr widgets show what is coming and what is in the queue, with posters - Widgets: a Seerr widget shows requests in Overseerr or Jellyseerr, who asked and whether they arrived - Widgets: qBittorrent and SABnzbd widgets show downloads with progress, speed and time left - Widgets: Add a widget opens a picker you can search, and new kinds carry a New badge in the Catalogue - Translations: the widget picker and a few Inbox messages no longer show English in the other languages

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the NextDash web interface

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: Persistent storage path for NextDash data (bookmarks, settings)

Config.Name: Write token
Config.Description: Optional. Require this token in the X-NextDash-Token header on every write. Leave empty for an open instance on a trusted network.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional. Addresses and CIDR ranges whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed, comma-separated — set this if nextDash sits behind a reverse proxy, so rate limits count per visitor instead of per proxy. Left empty the header is ignored.

Config.Name: Host proc
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the host /proc here for the Processor and Memory widgets. Host path: /proc

Config.Name: Host proc variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/proc once the mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Host disks
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the array here for the Disks widget. Host path: /mnt — then name /mnt/user or /mnt/cache in the widget.

Config.Name: Host root variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/root once the disks mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the Docker socket here for the Containers widget. Host path: /var/run/docker.sock — read-only still exposes the daemon's whole read API, so use a socket proxy if that is too much.

Config.Name: Docker socket variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /var/run/docker.sock once the socket mount above is filled in. Unset, the Containers widget is hidden.

Config.Name: Docker actions
Config.Description: Optional. 1 lets the Containers view start, stop, update and remove containers; 0 keeps it read-only. A writable socket is root on the host, so set a write token as well.

Config.Name: Run as root
Config.Description: Optional. 1 keeps nextDash running as root, needed only when the Docker socket belongs to root's group (gid 0). Unraid's socket belongs to the docker group (gid 281), so leave this at 0 here.
